title: Every model case gets 120 s (owner decision 2026-11-27), suite and output budgets stay
goal: A cold first load no longer times out a model pack's first case and skips the rest of the pack
acceptance: Owner decision 2026-11-27 morning in chat: "ok" to raising the per-case time for the other packs too, replacing F-120-T05's "every other pack keeps the day limits" (2026-11-26)

Found 2026-11-27 night (stage four): at the 30 s day case limit italian-quality on gemma4:12b (30,005 ms) and code-review on devstral-small-2:24b (30,007 ms) timed out on their first, cold-load case; a timeout leaves consumption unverified, so Gauntlet skipped the other five cases of each pack

Chosen option, the smallest: modelLimits gives every model case max(day or slow-host case time, MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS), so 120 s (the time NERV gives one model call, as nerv-planner since F-120-T18) and 180 s on the coding, embedded and cad-3d runner packs; the suite and output budgets stay the day limits'. Not chosen: a first-case-only allowance (Gauntlet has one case limit per run, so it needs a release change)

Tests first: test/gauntlet.test.mjs F-120-T19 (every non-runner model pack, including a --only selection of cad-3d's knowledge cases, gets MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS with unchanged suite and output budgets). Two deliberate expectation changes from this decision: F-120-T05's test now expects MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS for the other packs, and the cross-consumer reuse test runs the other consumer under the same 120 s limits (a consumer on the release's plain day limits no longer reuses NERV's cached common evidence)
privacy: Code and tests only; no model call, device or service change.
escalation: Not verified on a real model: the next owner-approved run of italian-quality and code-review is the check

effort.basis: Done 2026-11-27: one rule in modelLimits, failing-first test, docs. Not a measurement.
